title: Spent 2 days trying to describe a mechanic to my AI agent, turns out I just needed math
author: lollyadorable4
selftext:
Been obsessed with Superliminal lately and wanted to recreate that perspective-scaling mechanic (pick up an object, point it at the sky, it scales based on distance from camera) in the game I’m building with AI.

Spent two days describing it in plain English, stuff like “as the object gets closer to your viewpoint it scales up proportionally” and the results were never right. Kept getting weird snapping/jumping behavior. Went back and rewatched the original gameplay and realized my description was just wrong. It’s actually a simple ratio: if the object starts at size S0 at distance D0, and moves to distance D1, the new size S1 is just S0/S1 = D0/D1.

So basically: One sentence. That’s it. lol  
Still have some jank with the raycast detection when the camera angle shifts, working through that now. But wanted to share because I think we undersell how much just being precise (like, actual-math precise) beats throwing more words at these AI agents.

comments.author: Lucky_Pangolin_3760

replies.author: lollyadorable4
replies.body: Tbh it depends. Most of the actual building (placing the rooms, texturing, positioning the assets) I did by hand in the editor, the agent just handled the mechanic logic once I gave it the right description. So not quite “one prompt, whole game,” more like normal game project with an assist on the parts I was stuck on.

replies.author: SanoKei
replies.body:
read the research papers instead of watching sensationalist media lol

China is winning on understanding how to make compute cheaper through caching and have found a lot of obvious improvements to the transformer architecture. They made ram fucking expensive for sure, but the compute costs are on the floor. They also have started creating lithography machines so it's completely over they can win on supply production in 2 to 5 years.

With a good harness, Deepseek v4 flash (around 6 cents for a million tokens) is surprisingly competent and really fast, not as fast as diffusion but still plenty fast.

Local models have gotten to a point where you could run a model better than GPT-4 for the cost of electricity. Harnesses make it better and claude code is open source, changing out the model through the environment config is easy.
